newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Residents evacuate as PNG volcano erupts again.
newsitem.headline: Residents evacuate as PNG volcano erupts again.

text.p: Papua New Guinea (PNG) officials said on Sunday that about 300 people had left the town of Rabaul since Friday after one of two active volcanoes erupted, spewing ash 4,000 metres into the air and opening a new lava chasm.

"They were given advice to move but they also moved on their own account because of the noise," national disaster and emergency services director Leith Anderson told Reuters. "It was rather frightening, apparently," he said.

Rabaul, a port town located on New Britain Island 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the PNG capital Port Moresby, was devastated in September 1994, when the two volcanoes on either side of the picturesque town erupted, forcing the evacuation of its 30,000 residents.
Five people died in the 1994 evacuation and during attempts to return to the town over the next few days to rescue belongings from gangs of looters.
An earthquake measuring 6.2 on the open-ended Richter scale shook Rabaul in August last year. There was another eruption last May which Anderson said was more severe than Friday's rumbling.

Anderson described Friday's eruption at the Tavurvur volcano as moderately active. It lasted nearly three hours and led to the evacuation of some residents from Matupit Island, close to the town's former airstrip.
"There was a major lava flow which occurred about one kilometre (0.63 miles) along from the eastern side of the volcano which hadn't been there before," Anderson said.
"It was still flowing about two hours ago but not as fast as it was originally," he said.
